title: Scholastica's storm
hook: Benedict's sister prays for rain so he'll stay and talk, and a storm keeps him

segments.voice: Yesterday, Benedict left Rome for a cave and wrote a rule for monks. Your line was listen, with the ear of the heart. Who did you really hear? Day seven hundred eighty-seven.
screen: `LISTEN, WITH THE EAR OF THE HEART.`

segments.voice: Supper is finished. The candles are low. A brother and a sister sit across a table in a small house near his monastery, and they have talked all day about God. In the story, this is their custom: she comes to see him once a year, and they spend the whole day in praise and holy conversation. Now it's dark. She asks him to stay the night and keep talking until morning. He says no. He's the man who wrote the rule, and he says he cannot spend the night outside his monastery. So the sister does something else. She folds her hands on the table, rests her head on them, and prays. The sky outside is clear. Today, the rule-maker meets a storm.
screen: `ONE DAY A YEAR, TALKING ABOUT GOD.`

segments.voice: The sister is Scholastica, and the story comes from Pope Gregory the Great, who wrote down the life of her brother Benedict. When Scholastica lifts her head, Gregory says, the thunder breaks, the lightning flashes, and the rain comes down so hard that Benedict and the brothers with him can't put a foot out the door. Benedict is upset. In Gregory's telling he says, more or less, God forgive you, sister, what have you done? And she answers him: I asked you, and you wouldn't listen. So I asked my God, and he listened. Now go, if you can. He can't. So they stay up all night and talk, and the story says they filled each other with holy conversation until dawn. Gregory stops to explain why her prayer won. He was the holier man, wasn't he? Gregory doesn't answer that way. He quotes the letter of John: "God is love." And then the line that gives us today's carry: she could do more, because she loved more. Notice what the story doesn't do. It doesn't say Benedict's rule was wrong. Yesterday's rule still stands. It says that on one night, love outweighed it. Gregory adds a quiet ending. Three days later, Benedict, standing in his cell, sees his sister's soul rise toward heaven like a dove. He has her buried in the tomb he had made ready for himself. That was the last time they talked.
screen: `I ASKED MY GOD, AND HE LISTENED.`
`SHE COULD DO MORE: SHE LOVED MORE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: stay longer with someone. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one person you usually leave a little early. The call you end first. The visit you cut short because there's a schedule, a rule, a reason. Picture them across the table. Don't fix anything. Just notice what you might hear if you stayed ten more minutes. If you pray, you can name them before God. If you don't, just hold their face in your mind for this sit. The bell holds the time.
Scholastica's storm. The night a sister's prayer kept her brother at the table, because, as Gregory tells it, she loved more.
Your line: she loved more. Today, with the person you named, stay past the point where you'd usually go. Ten minutes is enough. Day seven hundred eighty-seven.

howItsDone: Christians who keep the old calendar of saints remember Saint Scholastica as Benedict's sister, and Benedictine communities keep her feast and retell the story of the storm.

fork.setup: you're Benedict. you wrote the rule, and you won't spend a night outside your monastery. your sister, who visits once a year, asks you to stay and talk all night. what do you do?
options: stay. it's one night, and she's your sister.
say no, and get ready to go back.
send the brothers back and stay alone.
fork.reveal: he says no. then she prays, the storm comes, and he can't leave. "I asked you, and you wouldn't listen. I asked my God, and he listened."

original.script: illa plus potuit, quae amplius amavit
original.say: IL-la ploos POH-too-it, kweh am-PLEE-us a-MAH-wit
original.note: Latin, from Gregory's Dialogues: she could do more, who loved more.

trapdoor: what you thought: a miracle about the weather.
what it means: a sister asks her brother to stay, he won't, and her prayer brings a storm that keeps him at the table all night.
what a scholar hears: Gregory's own explanation. he quotes "God is love" and says she could do more because she loved more.

sources.quoted: illa plus potuit, quae amplius amavit

notes: Paraphrased from Gregory, Dialogues 2.33–34: yearly visit, house near the monastery, refusal to stay outside the cell, prayer with head on hands, storm, 'God forgive you, sister', her reply, the all-night talk, the dove three days later, burial in Benedict's own tomb. Confirm each detail.

Latin original 'illa plus potuit, quae amplius amavit': confirm the exact wording against a critical edition. Gregory cites 1 John 4:16 ('God is love' appears in 4:8 and 4:16); confirm which verse he quotes.
The line 'She seems to have known it' is a gentle reading, not in Gregory; confirm or cut.
howItsDone: confirm Anglican and Orthodox commemorations of Scholastica before keeping them.
